newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson, financials lift Swedish shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson, financials lift Swedish shares higher.

text.p: The Swedish stock market rose 0.70 percent on Thursday encouraged by heavyweight Ericsson and shares which are sensitive to interest rates.
Share indexes stuttered half an hour before the close when New York wavered but later recovered on day volume of 3.47 billion crowns.
"We saw a fair interest in the financial sector, particularly towards the close, and that gave the index a push," said a broker.
Ericsson was stronger on gains in New York overnight, its B-share advancing four to 201 in the day's highest turnover of 580 million crowns.
Astra quickly shrugged off any negative effects of a newspaper article about the possible side-effects of its ulcer drug Losec, and the share climbed 1.50 to 313.
"Astra has a presentation for investers tomorrow in New York and I think there must be some who have lifted the share ahead of the expiry tomorrow of index options," said one broker.

Rate-sensitive stock was firm. The banking and insurance sector index rose one percent while building and property put on 1.5 percent. Skandia contributed with a 6.50 crown rise to 204.50 and Handelsbanken-A closed four up at 179.
Skanska's B-share headed again towards 300 closing 4.50 crowns up ahead of nine-month results on Friday.

Atlas Copco A rose four to 144.50 partly on a nine-month report above expectations. Elekta's B-share rose six to 260 after the decision to merge its radiation therapy activities with those of Philips Radiation Therapy.
